```
     1→# QMD Deep Agent Guide
     2→
     3→> **QMD** — Query Markup Documents. An on-device search engine for everything you need to remember. Index your markdown notes, meeting transcripts, documentation, and knowledge bases. Search with keywords or natural language. Ideal for agentic flows.
     4→>
     5→> Repository: [tobi/qmd](https://github.com/tobi/qmd) | License: MIT | Language: TypeScript | Runtime: Bun
     6→
     7→---
     8→
     9→## Table of Contents
    10→
    11→1. [Architecture Overview](#architecture-overview)
    12→2. [Installation](#installation)
    13→3. [Collection Management](#collection-management)
    14→4. [Vector Embeddings](#vector-embeddings)
    15→5. [Context Metadata](#context-metadata)
    16→6. [Search Modes](#search-modes)
    17→7. [Output Formats](#output-formats)
    18→8. [Document Retrieval](#document-retrieval)
    19→9. [MCP Server Integration](#mcp-server-integration)
    20→10. [Index Maintenance](#index-maintenance)
    21→11. [Data Storage & Schema](#data-storage--schema)
    22→12. [Search Pipeline Internals](#search-pipeline-internals)
    23→13. [Model Configuration](#model-configuration)
    24→14. [Score Interpretation](#score-interpretation)
    25→15. [Known Issues & Bugs](#known-issues--bugs)
    26→16. [Practical Tips & Patterns](#practical-tips--patterns)
    27→17. [CLI Reference](#cli-reference)
    28→18. [MCP Tool Reference](#mcp-tool-reference)
    29→19. [Environment Variables](#environment-variables)
    30→
    31→---
    32→
    33→## Architecture Overview
    34→
    35→QMD combines three search strategies — all running locally via `node-llama-cpp` with GGUF models:
    36→
    37→| Strategy | Engine | Model | Latency |
    38→|----------|--------|-------|---------|
    39→| **BM25 keyword search** | SQLite FTS5 | None (pure text) | ~30ms |
    40→| **Vector semantic search** | sqlite-vec | EmbeddingGemma 300M | ~2s |
    41→| **Deep hybrid search** | FTS5 + sqlite-vec + LLM | All 3 models | ~10s |
    42→
    43→The deep search pipeline:
    44→
    45→```
    46→User Query
    47→    |
    48→    +---> Query Expansion (fine-tuned 1.7B LLM) --> 2 alternative queries
    49→    +---> Original Query (x2 weight)
    50→    |
    51→    v
    52→For each query (original + expanded):
    53→    +---> BM25 (FTS5)
    54→    +---> Vector Search (cosine similarity)
    55→    |
    56→    v
    57→RRF Fusion (k=60) + Top-rank Bonus
    58→    |
    59→    v
    60→Top 30 candidates --> LLM Re-ranking (qwen3-reranker, yes/no + logprobs)
    61→    |
    62→    v
    63→Position-Aware Blend --> Final ranked results
    64→```
    65→
    66→---
    67→
    68→## Installation
    69→
    70→### Global install (recommended)
    71→
    72→```bash
    73→bun install -g github:tobi/qmd
    74→```
    75→
    76→Ensure `~/.bun/bin` is in your `PATH`.
    77→
    78→### Development install
    79→
    80→```bash
    81→git clone https://github.com/tobi/qmd
    82→cd qmd
    83→bun install
    84→bun link
    85→```
    86→
    87→### System requirements
    88→
    89→- **Bun** >= 1.0.0
    90→- **macOS**: Homebrew SQLite for extension support — `brew install sqlite`
    91→- **Disk**: ~2.1 GB for all three GGUF models (auto-downloaded on first use)
    92→
    93→---
    94→
    95→## Collection Management
    96→
    97→Collections are named indexes pointing to directories of markdown files.
    98→
    99→### Create a collection
   100→
   101→```bash
   102→# Index current directory
   103→qmd collection add . --name myproject
   104→
   105→# Index a specific directory with custom glob
   106→qmd collection add ~/Documents/notes --name notes --mask "**/*.md"
   107→
   108→# The --mask defaults to **/*.md if omitted
   109→qmd collection add /path/to/docs --name docs
   110→```
   111→
   112→### List collections
   113→
   114→```bash
   115→qmd collection list
   116→```
   117→
   118→Output includes: name, file count, path, last update time, context count.
   119→
   120→### List files in a collection
   121→
   122→```bash
   123→# List all collections
   124→qmd ls
   125→
   126→# List files in a collection
   127→qmd ls notes
   128→
   129→# List files in a subfolder
   130→qmd ls notes/subfolder
   131→```
   132→
   133→Output: file path, size, last modified timestamp.
   134→
   135→### Rename a collection
   136→
   137→```bash
   138→qmd collection rename old-name new-name
   139→```
   140→
   141→### Remove a collection
   142→
   143→```bash
   144→qmd collection remove myproject
   145→```
   146→
   147→This removes the collection metadata and indexed content from the database but does **not** delete the original files.
   148→
   149→---
   150→
   151→## Vector Embeddings
   152→
   153→Embeddings enable semantic search (`vsearch`) and improve deep search (`query`).
   154→
   155→### Generate embeddings
   156→
   157→```bash
   158→# Embed all documents (skips already-embedded)
   159→qmd embed
   160→
   161→# Force re-embed everything
   162→qmd embed -f
   163→```
   164→
   165→**Chunking parameters** (hardcoded):
   166→- **Chunk size**: 800 tokens
   167→- **Overlap**: 15% (120 tokens)
   168→- **Format**: Each chunk is formatted as `"title: {title} | text: {content}"`
   169→
   170→### First-run model download
   171→
   172→On first `embed`, QMD auto-downloads the EmbeddingGemma model (~314 MB) from HuggingFace. The download is a one-time cost — the model is cached at `~/.cache/qmd/models/`.
   173→
   174→---
   175→
   176→## Context Metadata
   177→
   178→Contexts are descriptive text strings attached to collection paths. They appear in search results alongside documents and help the search pipeline understand what a collection or path contains.
   179→
   180→### Add context
   181→
   182→```bash
   183→# Context for a collection root
   184→qmd context add qmd://notes "Personal notes and ideas"
   185→
   186→# Context for a subfolder
   187→qmd context add qmd://docs/api "API documentation and references"
   188→
   189→# Context for current directory (auto-resolves to qmd:// path)
   190→cd ~/notes && qmd context add "Personal notes and ideas"
   191→
   192→# Global context (applies to all collections)
   193→qmd context add / "Knowledge base for my projects"
   194→```
   195→
   196→### List contexts
   197→
   198→```bash
   199→qmd context list
   200→```
   201→
   202→### Remove context
   203→
   204→```bash
   205→qmd context rm qmd://notes/old
   206→```
   207→
   208→### How context appears in output
   209→
   210→Every search result and `get` output includes a `Context:` line showing the most specific matching context for that document's path. This helps agents understand what kind of content they're looking at without reading the full document.
   211→
   212→---
   213→
   214→## Search Modes
   215→
   216→QMD provides three search commands with increasing sophistication:
   217→
   218→### 1. `search` — BM25 Keyword Search
   219→
   220→**Speed**: ~30ms | **Models**: None | **Best for**: Exact keyword matching, known terms
   221→
   222→```bash
   223→qmd search "authentication flow"
   224→qmd search "error handling" -n 10
   225→qmd search "API" -c notes --min-score 0.3
   226→```
   227→
   228→Uses SQLite FTS5 under the hood. Fast and precise for exact terms but cannot find semantic matches (e.g., searching "login" won't find documents about "authentication").
   229→
   230→### 2. `vsearch` — Vector Semantic Search
   231→
   232→**Speed**: ~2s | **Models**: EmbeddingGemma 300M | **Best for**: Conceptual similarity, natural language queries
   233→
   234→```bash
   235→qmd vsearch "how to deploy the application"
   236→qmd vsearch "what are the error handling patterns" -n 10
   237→```
   238→
   239→Converts the query to an embedding vector and finds documents with similar meaning via cosine similarity. Can find relevant documents even when vocabulary differs. Requires `qmd embed` to have been run first.
   240→
   241→### 3. `query` — Deep Hybrid Search (Recommended)
   242→
   243→**Speed**: ~10s | **Models**: All 3 | **Best for**: Best quality results, complex questions
   244→
   245→```bash
   246→qmd query "how does the guardian state machine handle errors" -n 5
   247→qmd query "quarterly planning process" --min-score 0.4
   248→```
   249→
   250→The full pipeline:
   251→1. **Query expansion**: LLM generates 2 alternative phrasings
   252→2. **Parallel retrieval**: Each query runs against both BM25 and vector indexes
   253→3. **RRF fusion**: Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines all result lists
   254→4. **LLM re-ranking**: Qwen3 reranker scores top 30 candidates
   255→5. **Position-aware blending**: Final score balances retrieval confidence with reranker judgment
   256→
   257→On first run, downloads both the query-expansion model (~1.2 GB) and reranker model (~639 MB).
   258→
   259→### Common search options
   260→
   261→| Flag | Description | Default |
   262→|------|-------------|---------|
   263→| `-n <num>` | Number of results | 5 (search), 20 (--files/--json) |
   264→| `-c, --collection <name>` | Restrict to a collection | All collections |
   265→| `--all` | Return all matches | Off |
   266→| `--min-score <num>` | Minimum score threshold (0.0-1.0) | 0 |
   267→| `--full` | Show full document content | Snippet only |
   268→| `--line-numbers` | Add line numbers to output | Off |
   269→
   270→---
   271→
   272→## Output Formats
   273→
   274→QMD supports 6 output formats for search results. The default is a colorized CLI format.
   275→
   276→### Default (colorized terminal)
   277→
   278→```bash
   279→qmd search "guardian state machine"
   280→```
   281→
   282→```
   283→_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/2-1-guardian-state-machine.md:1 #b3f1e0
   284→Title: Story 2.1: Guardian State Machine
   285→Context: Pause AI Financial Guardian - a hackathon project with...
   286→Score:  100%
   287→
   288→@@ -1,4 @@ (0 before, 10 after)
   289→...matched snippet with query terms highlighted...
   290→```
   291→
   292→Fields: path (collection-relative), docid (`#` + 6-char hash), title (first heading or filename), context, score (color-coded), snippet.
   293→
   294→### `--json` — JSON output
   295→
   296→```bash
   297→qmd search "guardian" --json -n 3
   298→```
   299→
   300→Returns a JSON array of result objects with `docid`, `path`, `title`, `context`, `score`, and `snippet` fields. Ideal for programmatic consumption and agentic workflows.
   301→
   302→### `--csv` — CSV output
   303→
   304→```bash
   305→qmd search "guardian" --csv
   306→```
   307→
   308→Comma-separated values with headers.
   309→
   310→### `--xml` — XML output
   311→
   312→```bash
   313→qmd search "guardian" --xml
   314→```
   315→
   316→### `--md` — Markdown output
   317→
   318→```bash
   319→qmd search "guardian" --md
   320→```
   321→
   322→Formatted markdown with headers, code blocks, and score badges.
   323→
   324→### `--files` — File listing (compact)
   325→
   326→```bash
   327→qmd search "guardian" --files
   328→```
   329→
   330→Returns: `docid,score,filepath,context` — one line per result. Default 20 results instead of 5. Best for getting a quick overview of matching files.
   331→
   332→---
   333→
   334→## Document Retrieval
   335→
   336→### Get a single document
   337→
   338→```bash
   339→# By collection-relative path
   340→qmd get "docs/api-reference.md"
   341→
   342→# By virtual path (with qmd:// prefix)
   343→qmd get qmd://pause/docs/api-reference.md
   344→
   345→# By docid (shown in search results as #xxxxxx)
   346→qmd get "#abc123"
   347→```
   348→
   349→### Get with line range
   350→
   351→```bash
   352→# Start from line 50
   353→qmd get "docs/guide.md" --from 50
   354→
   355→# Start from line 50, get 100 lines
   356→qmd get "docs/guide.md:50" -l 100
   357→
   358→# Shorthand: path:line syntax
   359→qmd get "docs/guide.md:50" -l 100
   360→```
   361→
   362→### Get with line numbers
   363→
   364→```bash
   365→qmd get "docs/guide.md" --line-numbers
   366→```
   367→
   368→### Get multiple documents
   369→
   370→```bash
   371→# By glob pattern
   372→qmd multi-get "docs/*.md"
   373→
   374→# By comma-separated list
   375→qmd multi-get "doc1.md, doc2.md, doc3.md"
   376→
   377→# With size limit (skip files > 20KB)
   378→qmd multi-get "docs/*.md" --max-bytes 20480
   379→
   380→# Limit lines per file
   381→qmd multi-get "docs/*.md" -l 50
   382→
   383→# With output format
   384→qmd multi-get "docs/*.md" --json
   385→```
   386→
   387→**Default max-bytes**: 10240 (10 KB). Files larger than this are skipped unless you increase the limit.
   388→
   389→### Virtual path prefix
   390→
   391→QMD uses `qmd://` virtual paths:
   392→- `qmd://collection-name/path/to/file.md` — full virtual path
   393→- The `qmd://` prefix is **required** for `multi-get` glob patterns
   394→- The `qmd://` prefix is **optional** for `get` (plain paths work too)
   395→
   396→---
   397→
   398→## MCP Server Integration
   399→
   400→QMD exposes 6 tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
   401→
   402→### Starting the MCP server
   403→
   404→```bash
   405→# stdio transport (default, launched as subprocess by MCP clients)
   406→qmd mcp
   407→
   408→# HTTP transport (shared, long-lived server)
   409→qmd mcp --http                    # localhost:8181
   410→qmd mcp --http --port 8080        # custom port
   411→
   412→# Background daemon
   413→qmd mcp --http --daemon           # start, writes PID to ~/.cache/qmd/mcp.pid
   414→qmd mcp stop                      # stop daemon
   415→```
   416→
   417→The HTTP server exposes:
   418→- `POST /mcp` — MCP Streamable HTTP (JSON, stateless)
   419→- `GET /health` — liveness check with uptime
   420→
   421→**Performance benefit**: HTTP daemon keeps models loaded in VRAM across requests. Embedding/reranking contexts are disposed after 5 min idle and transparently recreated on next request (~1s penalty).
   422→
   423→### Claude Desktop configuration
   424→
   425→`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`:
   426→
   427→```json
   428→{
   429→  "mcpServers": {
   430→    "qmd": {
   431→      "command": "qmd",
   432→      "args": ["mcp"]
   433→    }
   434→  }
   435→}
   436→```
   437→
   438→### Claude Code configuration
   439→
   440→Plugin install (recommended):
   441→
   442→```bash
   443→claude marketplace add tobi/qmd
   444→claude plugin add qmd@qmd
   445→```
   446→
   447→Or manual MCP in `~/.claude/settings.json`:
   448→
   449→```json
   450→{
   451→  "mcpServers": {
   452→    "qmd": {
   453→      "command": "qmd",
   454→      "args": ["mcp"]
   455→    }
   456→  }
   457→}
   458→```
   459→
   460→---
   461→
   462→## Index Maintenance
   463→
   464→### Check status
   465→
   466→```bash
   467→qmd status
   468→```
   469→
   470→Shows: index location, size, MCP server status (if running), document count, vector count, last update, collections with file counts and contexts.
   471→
   472→### Re-index collections
   473→
   474→```bash
   475→# Re-scan files for changes (incremental — only processes changed files)
   476→qmd update
   477→
   478→# Git pull first, then re-index
   479→qmd update --pull
   480→```
   481→
   482→The update uses content hashing for change detection — only new or modified files are re-indexed.
   483→
   484→### Cleanup
   485→
   486→```bash
   487→qmd cleanup
   488→```
   489→
   490→Removes cache, orphaned data, and vacuums the SQLite database.
   491→
   492→---
   493→
   494→## Data Storage & Schema
   495→
   496→**Index location**: `~/.cache/qmd/index.sqlite`
   497→
   498→**SQLite tables**:
   499→
   500→| Table | Purpose |
   501→|-------|---------|
   502→| `collections` | Indexed directories with name and glob patterns |
   503→| `path_contexts` | Context descriptions by virtual path (`qmd://...`) |
   504→| `documents` | Markdown content with metadata and docid (6-char hash) |
   505→| `documents_fts` | FTS5 full-text index (powers BM25 search) |
   506→| `content_vectors` | Embedding chunks: hash, seq, pos, 800 tokens each |
   507→| `vectors_vec` | sqlite-vec vector index (hash_seq key) |
   508→| `llm_cache` | Cached LLM responses (query expansion, rerank scores) |
   509→
   510→**Model storage**: `~/.cache/qmd/models/`
   511→
   512→| Model File | Size | Purpose |
   513→|------------|------|---------|
   514→| `hf_ggml-org_embeddinggemma-300M-Q8_0.gguf` | 314 MB | Vector embeddings |
   515→| `hf_tobil_qmd-query-expansion-1.7B-q4_k_m.gguf` | 1.2 GB | Query expansion |
   516→| `hf_ggml-org_qwen3-reranker-0.6b-q8_0.gguf` | 610 MB | Re-ranking |
   517→| **Total** | **~2.1 GB** | |
   518→
   519→---
   520→
   521→## Search Pipeline Internals
   522→
   523→### Score Normalization
   524→
   525→| Backend | Raw Score | Conversion | Range |
   526→|---------|-----------|------------|-------|
   527→| FTS (BM25) | SQLite FTS5 BM25 | `Math.abs(score)` | 0 to ~25+ |
   528→| Vector | Cosine distance | `1 / (1 + distance)` | 0.0 to 1.0 |
   529→| Reranker | LLM 0-10 rating | `score / 10` | 0.0 to 1.0 |
   530→
   531→### Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
   532→
   533→The `query` command fuses results from multiple retrieval runs:
   534→
   535→```
   536→score = sum(1 / (k + rank + 1))    where k = 60
   537→```
   538→
   539→- Original query gets **x2 weight** in the fusion
   540→- Top-rank bonus: `+0.05` for documents ranking #1 in any list, `+0.02` for #2-3
   541→
   542→### Position-Aware Blending
   543→
   544→After RRF fusion and LLM re-ranking, the final score blends both signals based on rank:
   545→
   546→| RRF Rank | Retrieval Weight | Reranker Weight | Rationale |
   547→|----------|-----------------|-----------------|-----------|
   548→| 1-3 | 75% | 25% | Preserves exact keyword matches |
   549→| 4-10 | 60% | 40% | Balanced |
   550→| 11+ | 40% | 60% | Trust reranker more for uncertain matches |
   551→
   552→**Why**: Pure RRF can dilute exact matches when expanded queries diverge. The top-rank bonus and position-aware blending preserve high-confidence retrieval results while letting the reranker rescue relevant documents that keyword search missed.
   553→
   554→### Embedding Format
   555→
   556→EmbeddingGemma uses task-prefixed prompts:
   557→- **Queries**: `"task: search result | query: {query}"`
   558→- **Documents**: `"title: {title} | text: {content}"`
   559→
   560→---
   561→
   562→## Model Configuration
   563→
   564→Models are defined in `src/llm.ts` as HuggingFace URIs:
   565→
   566→```typescript
   567→const DEFAULT_EMBED_MODEL =
   568→  "hf:ggml-org/embeddinggemma-300M-GGUF/embeddinggemma-300M-Q8_0.gguf";
   569→const DEFAULT_RERANK_MODEL =
   570→  "hf:ggml-org/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-Q8_0-GGUF/qwen3-reranker-0.6b-q8_0.gguf";
   571→const DEFAULT_GENERATE_MODEL =
   572→  "hf:tobil/qmd-query-expansion-1.7B-gguf/qmd-query-expansion-1.7B-q4_k_m.gguf";
   573→```
   574→
   575→Models are auto-downloaded from HuggingFace on first use and cached in `~/.cache/qmd/models/`.
   576→
   577→| Model | Architecture | Quantization | Purpose |
   578→|-------|-------------|-------------|---------|
   579→| EmbeddingGemma 300M | Embedding | Q8_0 | Convert text to vectors for similarity search |
   580→| qmd-query-expansion 1.7B | Qwen3 (fine-tuned) | Q4_K_M | Generate query variations for broader recall |
   581→| Qwen3 Reranker 0.6B | Qwen3 (cross-encoder) | Q8_0 | Score document-query relevance (yes/no + logprobs) |
   582→
   583→---
   584→
   585→## Score Interpretation
   586→
   587→Scores displayed as percentages in output:
   588→
   589→| Score | Meaning | Action |
   590→|-------|---------|--------|
   591→| **80% - 100%** | Highly relevant | Always show to user |
   592→| **50% - 80%** | Moderately relevant | Include if few high-quality results |
   593→| **20% - 50%** | Somewhat relevant | Only if user wants exhaustive coverage |
   594→| **0% - 20%** | Low relevance | Usually skip |
   595→
   596→**Color coding** in default terminal output:
   597→- Green: > 70%
   598→- Yellow: > 40%
   599→- Dim: below 40%
   600→
   601→---
   602→
   603→## Known Issues & Bugs
   604→
   605→Issues discovered during hands-on testing (tested against a 553-file codebase with 1881 vector chunks):
   606→
   607→### 1. `multi-get` does not support docids
   608→
   609→**Severity**: Medium | **Workaround**: Use `get` for individual docids
   610→
   611→```bash
   612→# WORKS — get by docid
   613→qmd get "#ca37dc"
   614→
   615→# BROKEN — multi-get with docids returns "File not found"
   616→qmd multi-get "#ca37dc,#db75e1"
   617→```
   618→
   619→The README documents `qmd multi-get "doc1.md, doc2.md, #abc123"` as valid, but docids in comma-separated lists silently fail. Only glob patterns and file paths work with `multi-get`.
   620→
   621→### 2. Hyphenated terms return 0 BM25 results
   622→
   623→**Severity**: Low | **Workaround**: Search without hyphens or use `vsearch`/`query`
   624→
   625→```bash
   626→# Returns 0 results despite files containing "better-auth"
   627→qmd search "better-auth"
   628→
   629→# Workaround: search without hyphen
   630→qmd search "better auth"
   631→```
   632→
   633→The FTS5 tokenizer appears to split on hyphens, so `"better-auth"` doesn't match as a phrase.
   634→
   635→### 3. Unicode accent handling produces false positives
   636→
   637→**Severity**: Low | **Workaround**: Be aware of spurious high-score results for accented terms
   638→
   639→```bash
   640→# Returns unrelated documents with 85-86% scores
   641→qmd search "resume"   # matches "resume" fragments in unrelated content
   642→```
   643→
   644→The BM25 tokenizer likely strips accents, causing `"resume"` to match common word fragments.
   645→
   646→### 4. No `--version` flag
   647→
   648→**Severity**: Cosmetic | `qmd --version` prints the help text and exits with code 1.
   649→
   650→### 5. No per-subcommand help
   651→
   652→**Severity**: Cosmetic | All `--help` invocations (`qmd search --help`, `qmd collection add --help`, etc.) print the same unified help text.
   653→
   654→---
   655→
   656→## Practical Tips & Patterns
   657→
   658→### For AI Agents
   659→
   660→```bash
   661→# Get structured results for LLM consumption
   662→qmd search "authentication" --json -n 10
   663→
   664→# List all relevant files above a threshold
   665→qmd query "error handling" --all --files --min-score 0.4
   666→
   667→# Retrieve full document content by docid from search results
   668→qmd get "#abc123" --full
   669→
   670→# Batch retrieve matching docs for context injection
   671→qmd multi-get "qmd://collection/docs/*.md" --max-bytes 20480
   672→```
   673→
   674→### Recommended workflow
   675→
   676→1. **Start with keyword search** — fast, precise for known terms:
   677→   ```bash
   678→   qmd search "specific function name" -n 10
   679→   ```
   680→
   681→2. **Escalate to semantic search** if keywords miss:
   682→   ```bash
   683→   qmd vsearch "describe the concept you're looking for"
   684→   ```
   685→
   686→3. **Use deep search for complex questions** requiring best quality:
   687→   ```bash
   688→   qmd query "how does X work in the context of Y" --min-score 0.3
   689→   ```
   690→
   691→4. **Retrieve full documents** for the results you need:
   692→   ```bash
   693→   qmd get "#docid" --full --line-numbers
   694→   ```
   695→
   696→### Collection strategy
   697→
   698→- **One collection per project/domain** — keeps search focused
   699→- **Add context to every collection** — dramatically improves result quality
   700→- **Use `--min-score` with `--all`** — gets exhaustive results while filtering noise
   701→- **Run `qmd embed` after indexing** — required for `vsearch` and improves `query`
   702→- **Run `qmd update` periodically** — picks up new/changed files incrementally
   703→
   704→### Performance tips
   705→
   706→- **Use HTTP daemon** for repeated searches — avoids model reload latency:
   707→  ```bash
   708→  qmd mcp --http --daemon
   709→  ```
   710→- **BM25 is instant** — use `search` when you know the exact terms
   711→- **Vector search is ~2s** — acceptable for interactive use
   712→- **Deep search is ~10s** — batch/background use recommended
   713→- **`--files` output** is most compact — best for agent file discovery
   714→- **`--json` output** is most structured — best for agent result parsing
   715→
   716→### Index path conventions
   717→
   718→```
   719→qmd://collection-name/relative/path/to/file.md
   720→       ^               ^
   721→       collection       path relative to collection root
   722→```
   723→
   724→- Always use `qmd://` prefix for `multi-get` glob patterns
   725→- Omit `qmd://` prefix for `get` (plain paths work)
   726→- Docids are 6-character hashes prefixed with `#` (e.g., `#b3f1e0`)
   727→
   728→---
   729→
   730→## CLI Reference
   731→
   732→### Complete command list
   733→
   734→```
   735→qmd collection add [path] --name <name> --mask <pattern>  Create/index collection
   736→qmd collection list                                        List all collections
   737→qmd collection remove <name>                               Remove a collection
   738→qmd collection rename <old> <new>                          Rename a collection
   739→qmd ls [collection[/path]]                                 List collections or files
   740→qmd context add [path] "text"                              Add context for path
   741→qmd context list                                           List all contexts
   742→qmd context rm <path>                                      Remove context
   743→qmd get <file>[:line] [-l N] [--from N]                    Get document
   744→qmd multi-get <pattern> [-l N] [--max-bytes N]             Get multiple documents
   745→qmd status                                                 Show index status
   746→qmd update [--pull]                                        Re-index (--pull: git pull first)
   747→qmd embed [-f]                                             Create vector embeddings
   748→qmd cleanup                                                Remove cache, vacuum DB
   749→qmd query <query>                                          Hybrid search + reranking
   750→qmd search <query>                                         BM25 keyword search
   751→qmd vsearch <query>                                        Vector semantic search
   752→qmd mcp                                                    Start MCP server (stdio)
   753→qmd mcp --http [--port N]                                  Start MCP server (HTTP)
   754→qmd mcp --http --daemon                                    Start MCP server as daemon
   755→qmd mcp stop                                               Stop MCP daemon
   756→```
   757→
   758→### Global options
   759→
   760→| Flag | Description | Default |
   761→|------|-------------|---------|
   762→| `--index <name>` | Use custom index name | `index` |
   763→
   764→### Search options
   765→
   766→| Flag | Description | Default |
   767→|------|-------------|---------|
   768→| `-n <num>` | Number of results | 5 (20 for --files/--json) |
   769→| `-c, --collection <name>` | Filter to collection | All |
   770→| `--all` | Return all matches | Off |
   771→| `--min-score <num>` | Minimum score (0.0-1.0) | 0 |
   772→| `--full` | Full document content | Snippet |
   773→| `--line-numbers` | Show line numbers | Off |
   774→| `--json` | JSON output | Off |
   775→| `--csv` | CSV output | Off |
   776→| `--md` | Markdown output | Off |
   777→| `--xml` | XML output | Off |
   778→| `--files` | Compact file listing | Off |
   779→
   780→### Multi-get options
   781→
   782→| Flag | Description | Default |
   783→|------|-------------|---------|
   784→| `-l <num>` | Max lines per file | Unlimited |
   785→| `--max-bytes <num>` | Skip files larger than N | 10240 |
   786→| `--json/--csv/--md/--xml/--files` | Output format | Default |
   787→
   788→---
   789→
   790→## MCP Tool Reference
   791→
   792→Six tools exposed via the MCP server:
   793→
   794→### `qmd_search`
   795→
   796→BM25 keyword search. Supports `query` (string), `n` (number), `collection` (string), `minScore` (number) parameters.
   797→
   798→### `qmd_vector_search`
   799→
   800→Semantic vector search. Same parameters as `qmd_search`. Requires embeddings to exist.
   801→
   802→### `qmd_deep_search`
   803→
   804→Full hybrid pipeline: query expansion + BM25 + vector + RRF fusion + LLM re-ranking. Same parameters as `qmd_search`.
   805→
   806→### `qmd_get`
   807→
   808→Retrieve a single document by path or docid. Supports `path` (string, e.g. `"qmd://pause/docs/guide.md"` or `"#abc123"`), `lineOffset` (number), `maxLines` (number).
   809→
   810→Includes fuzzy matching suggestions if the exact path is not found.
   811→
   812→### `qmd_multi_get`
   813→
   814→Retrieve multiple documents by glob pattern or comma-separated paths. Supports `pattern` (string), `maxLines` (number), `maxBytes` (number).
   815→
   816→**Note**: Docids do not work in `multi_get` — use file paths or glob patterns only.
   817→
   818→### `qmd_status`
   819→
   820→Returns index health, document/vector counts, collection list, and MCP server status.
   821→
   822→---
   823→
   824→## Environment Variables
   825→
   826→| Variable | Default | Description |
   827→|----------|---------|-------------|
   828→| `XDG_CACHE_HOME` | `~/.cache` | Base directory for QMD cache (index, models) |
   829→| `NO_COLOR` | — | Disables colorized terminal output when set |
   830→
   831→---
   832→
   833→## Testing Checklist
   834→
   835→Use this checklist to validate a QMD installation:
   836→
   837→- [ ] **Collection**: `qmd collection add . --name test` indexes files
   838→- [ ] **Status**: `qmd status` shows collection with file count
   839→- [ ] **BM25**: `qmd search "known term"` returns relevant results
   840→- [ ] **Output formats**: `--json`, `--csv`, `--xml`, `--md`, `--files` all produce valid output
   841→- [ ] **Get by path**: `qmd get "collection/file.md"` returns document content
   842→- [ ] **Get by docid**: `qmd get "#xxxxxx"` returns document (docid from search results)
   843→- [ ] **Get with line range**: `qmd get "file.md:50" -l 100` returns correct slice
   844→- [ ] **Line numbers**: `qmd get "file.md" --line-numbers` prepends line numbers
   845→- [ ] **Multi-get glob**: `qmd multi-get "qmd://collection/docs/*.md"` returns multiple docs
   846→- [ ] **Context**: `qmd context add qmd://collection "description"` + verify in search output
   847→- [ ] **Embed**: `qmd embed` creates vector embeddings (downloads model on first run)
   848→- [ ] **Vector search**: `qmd vsearch "conceptual query"` returns semantic matches
   849→- [ ] **Deep search**: `qmd query "complex question"` runs full pipeline (downloads 2 models on first run)
   850→- [ ] **Collection filter**: `qmd search "term" -c collection-name` restricts results
   851→- [ ] **Min score**: `qmd search "term" --all --min-score 0.5` filters low-relevance results
   852→- [ ] **Update**: `qmd update` detects and re-indexes changed files
   853→- [ ] **MCP server**: `qmd mcp` starts stdio transport (test via MCP client)
   854→- [ ] **Cleanup**: `qmd cleanup` vacuums the database
   855→

 ## Common Use Cases
 
-### I need skills for my dependencies
-Use Quick Skill (`QS`) for each dependency. It resolves package names to repos automatically.
+### My agent keeps hallucinating API calls
+
+Your agent invents function signatures that don't exist. Generate a verified skill so it works from structural truth instead of guessing.
+
+```
+@Ferris QS https://github.com/org/library
+```
+
+The skill pins every function to its actual source location. Hallucinations stop.
+
+### I'm adopting a new library and need my agent to use it correctly
+
+You added a dependency but your agent doesn't know its API yet. Quick Skill resolves package names across npm, PyPI, and crates.io.
+
+```
+@Ferris QS cognee
+```
+
+Ferris resolves the package to its GitHub repo, extracts the public API, and generates a skill your agent can reference immediately.
+
+### I want my agent to understand my entire project stack
+
+Individual skills cover single libraries. Stack Skill maps how your dependencies interact — shared types, co-import patterns, integration points.
+
+```
+@Ferris SS
+```
+
+Ferris detects your manifests, ranks dependencies by significance, and generates a consolidated skill with cross-library integration patterns.
 
 ### I'm onboarding a large existing codebase
-Use Analyze Source (`AN`) to discover what to skill, then batch-create with Create Skill (`CS --batch`).
 
-### I maintain an OSS library
-Use Brief Skill (`BS`) + Create Skill (`CS`) for maximum quality. Export with `source_authority: official`.
+A brownfield repo with dozens of modules. You need to know what's worth skilling before you start.
+
+```
+@Ferris AN
+```
+
+Analyze Source scans the project, identifies skillable units, maps exports, and generates recommended briefs you can batch-create with `@Ferris CS --batch`.
+
+### I want the highest accuracy possible
+
+Quick mode reads source files. Forge mode adds AST parsing for structural truth. Deep mode goes further — QMD indexes your project's markdown (docs, changelogs, issues, migration guides) into searchable collections, then uses BM25 keyword search, vector semantic search, and LLM-powered re-ranking to surface context no other tool can find.
+
+```
+@Ferris SF    # Setup detects your tools and sets tier automatically
+```
+
+If `ast-grep` and `qmd` are available, Ferris activates Deep mode. Every skill gets AST-verified signatures (T1) enriched with deep knowledge search (T2) — deprecation warnings, breaking change history, common pitfalls surfaced by hybrid search across your indexed documentation.
+
+### I maintain an OSS library and want official skills
 
-### I want my agent to understand my whole project
-Use Stack Skill (`SS`) for a consolidated skill with cross-library integration patterns.
+You want maximum quality with full provenance for distribution. Use the full pipeline with Deep mode for the richest output.
+
+```
+@Ferris BS    # Scope and design the skill
+@Ferris CS    # Compile — AST extraction + QMD enrichment (Deep)
+@Ferris TS    # Verify completeness before publishing
+@Ferris EX    # Package for distribution
+```
+
+Export with `source_authority: official`. Consumers get verified skills that update with each release.
+
+### A dependency shipped breaking changes
+
+Your existing skill is now out of date. Audit detects the drift, Update regenerates while preserving your manual additions.
+
+```
+@Ferris AS    # Find what changed
+@Ferris US    # Regenerate — [MANUAL] sections survive
+@Ferris TS    # Verify the update
+```

    53→```

    55→```
    56→
    57→Ferris detects 8 significant dependencies, finds 5 co-import integration points. Generates a consolidated stack skill. The agent now knows: "When you modify the auth flow, update the Serwist cache exclusion at `src/sw.ts:L23`." Integration intelligence no other tool provides.

    59→---

    61→## Common Scenarios
    62→
    63→### Scenario A: Greenfield + BMM Integration
    64→
    65→BMAD user starts a new project. BMM architect suggests skill generation after retrospective.
    66→
    67→```

    73→

    93→
    94→No source code available — only documentation.
    95→

    97→
    98→---
    99→
   100→## Tips & Tricks
   101→
   102→### Progressive Capability
   103→
   104→Start with Quick mode (no setup required), upgrade to Forge (install ast-grep), then Deep (QMD already included). Each tier builds on the previous — you never lose capability.
   105→
   106→### Batch Operations
   107→
   108→Use `--batch` with `create-skill` and `test-skill` to process multiple skills at once. Progress is checkpointed — use `--continue` to resume if interrupted.
   109→
   110→### Stack Skills + Individual Skills
   111→
   112→Stack skills focus on integration patterns. Individual skills focus on API surface. Use both together for maximum coverage.
   113→
   114→### The Loop
   115→
   116→After each sprint's refactor, run `@Ferris US` to regenerate changed components. Export updates CLAUDE.md automatically. Skill generation becomes routine — like running tests.
   117→
   118→---
   119→
   120→## Troubleshooting
   121→
   122→### Common Issues
   123→
   124→**"Forge halted: ast-grep not found"**
   125→Install ast-grep to unlock Forge mode: <https://ast-grep.github.io>
   126→
   127→**"No brief found"**
   128→Run `@Ferris BS` first to create a skill brief, or use `@Ferris QS` for brief-less generation.
   129→
   130→**"Ecosystem check: official skill exists"**
   131→An official skill already exists for this package. Consider installing it with `npx skills add` instead of generating your own.
   132→
   133→**Quick mode skills have lower confidence**
   134→Quick mode reads source without AST analysis. Install ast-grep to upgrade to Forge mode for structural truth (T1 confidence).
   135→
   136→---
   137→
   138→## Getting More Help
   139→
   140→- Run `@Ferris SF` to check your current tier and tool availability
   141→- Review `forge-config.yaml` for runtime configuration
   142→- Check module configuration in your BMAD settings
   143→- Consult the broader BMAD documentation
   144→

 ## Common Use Cases
 
-### I need skills for my dependencies
-Use Quick Skill (`QS`) for each dependency. It resolves package names to repos automatically.
+### My agent keeps hallucinating API calls
+
+Your agent invents function signatures that don't exist. Generate a verified skill so it works from structural truth instead of guessing.
+
+```
+@Ferris QS https://github.com/org/library
+```
+
+The skill pins every function to its actual source location. Hallucinations stop.
+
+### I'm adopting a new library and need my agent to use it correctly
+
+You added a dependency but your agent doesn't know its API yet. Quick Skill resolves package names across npm, PyPI, and crates.io.
+
+```
+@Ferris QS cognee
+```
+
+Ferris resolves the package to its GitHub repo, extracts the public API, and generates a skill your agent can reference immediately.
+
+### I want my agent to understand my entire project stack
+
+Individual skills cover single libraries. Stack Skill maps how your dependencies interact — shared types, co-import patterns, integration points.
+
+```
+@Ferris SS
+```
+
+Ferris detects your manifests, ranks dependencies by significance, and generates a consolidated skill with cross-library integration patterns.
 
 ### I'm onboarding a large existing codebase
-Use Analyze Source (`AN`) to discover what to skill, then batch-create with Create Skill (`CS --batch`).
 
-### I maintain an OSS library
-Use Brief Skill (`BS`) + Create Skill (`CS`) for maximum quality. Export with `source_authority: official`.
+A brownfield repo with dozens of modules. You need to know what's worth skilling before you start.
+
+```
+@Ferris AN
+```
+
+Analyze Source scans the project, identifies skillable units, maps exports, and generates recommended briefs you can batch-create with `@Ferris CS --batch`.
+
+### I want the highest accuracy possible
+
+Quick mode reads source files. Forge mode adds AST parsing for structural truth. Deep mode goes further — QMD indexes your project's markdown (docs, changelogs, issues, migration guides) into searchable collections, then uses BM25 keyword search, vector semantic search, and LLM-powered re-ranking to surface context no other tool can find.
+
+```
+@Ferris SF    # Setup detects your tools and sets tier automatically
+```
+
+If `ast-grep` and `qmd` are available, Ferris activates Deep mode. Every skill gets AST-verified signatures (T1) enriched with deep knowledge search (T2) — deprecation warnings, breaking change history, common pitfalls surfaced by hybrid search across your indexed documentation.
+
+### I maintain an OSS library and want official skills
 
-### I want my agent to understand my whole project
-Use Stack Skill (`SS`) for a consolidated skill with cross-library integration patterns.
+You want maximum quality with full provenance for distribution. Use the full pipeline with Deep mode for the richest output.
+
+```
+@Ferris BS    # Scope and design the skill
+@Ferris CS    # Compile — AST extraction + QMD enrichment (Deep)
+@Ferris TS    # Verify completeness before publishing
+@Ferris EX    # Package for distribution
+```
+
+Export with `source_authority: official`. Consumers get verified skills that update with each release.
+
+### A dependency shipped breaking changes
+
+Your existing skill is now out of date. Audit detects the drift, Update regenerates while preserving your manual additions.
+
+```
+@Ferris AS    # Find what changed
+@Ferris US    # Regenerate — [MANUAL] sections survive
+@Ferris TS    # Verify the update
+```
